summary: One choice among two to four options that each need a title and a short description, shown as cards: Keep mine or Use the library's, a starting brand, a corner style. The whole card is the click target.

p.label: Which value should this change keep?

p.title: Use the library's
p.description: {color.harbor.700}, the value published in the library.

whenToUse: A decision where each option needs a line of explanation or a value to compare: resolving a conflict, picking a starting brand.
Two to four options. Side by side (horizontal, the default) when the reader compares them; they stack on their own when they no longer fit.
vertical when the descriptions are long or the options are a ranked list.
Put a TokenValue in description when the choice is between token values, so the reader sees what each card keeps.
hideLabel when the row around the group already asks the question; the legend stays the accessible name.
whenNotToUse: Options a short label explains on its own: use RadioGroup.
Switching a view or a mode that applies at once: use SegmentedControl.
Several options the reader can pick together: use Checkbox.
More than four options: use RadioGroup or Select.

dos.title: Titles are the choice, descriptions are the consequence
dos.text: The title says what the reader picks in a few words, the description says what happens or what it keeps.

dos.title: Ask the question in the legend
dos.text: The legend names the decision, as a question or a noun, so the cards read as answers.

donts.title: Cards for one-word options
donts.text: When the titles say it all and nothing needs comparing, cards take room for nothing. Use RadioGroup.

donts.title: Descriptions that repeat the title
donts.text: "Keep mine: keeps your value" says it twice. Show the value instead, or what changes.

p.label: Which value should this change keep?

accessibility: A fieldset with a legend around a Base UI RadioGroup: the legend names the group, each card is a radio named by its title.
Each card's description is linked to its radio with aria-describedby, so screen readers read it after the title. The group description and error are linked to the group.
Tab enters the group on the selected card and leaves it; arrow keys move the selection.
The selected card shows the checked radio, a Deep Harbor edge and the selected surface: never color alone.
A disabled card is skipped by the arrow keys and cannot be picked; say why in its description.
The focus ring (focus.ring.color) shows on the radio on keyboard focus only.
contentGuidelines: Legend: the decision, as a question or a noun, sentence case: "Which value should this change keep?", "Starting brand".
Title: a verb or a short name, a few words: "Keep mine", "Use the library's", "Ocean".
Description: one or two lines, the consequence or the value. No period after a lone value.
Error: what to do, not what went wrong: "Pick a value before you add it to the library."

anatomy.horizontal: Side by side, stacks when it no longer fits (default)
anatomy.card: One option: the whole card is the click target
anatomy.title: Title, names the radio
